rv.q: In the end, the veteran criminal turns out to be right: "Some get rich, some get caught, and sent away to dissuade the others from figuring it out. You want someone to 'explain it to you?' Here’s the wisdom: everything is what it seems. All the cards are in the deck.
And here's the welcome surprise: despite all the baggage, the art does manage to shine through. It's really very good...
Henry Johnson doesn't hit the sustained highs of those plays, but it's very, very good and highly entertaining.
You may leave the theater questioning your trust in humanity, but at least trust me when I say this is a play worth seeing.
The dialog is less compelling than Mamet's signature works, which take a lot of rehearsal to refine the playwright's intended cadences.

Unquestionably, the cast is fascinating to watch throughout the course of this drama, even though there are elements of dramatic tension that seem to be stifled by both scene breaks and the intermission.

Meaty performances and CODESIGN STUDIOS' sleekly austere set design are reasons to experience Henry Johnson, but how much you enjoy the play may be determined by how satisfactory you prefer your suspense.
So, OK, if one can put aside the politics of its creator and the venue's recent history, is this a show worth seeing? If you like Mamet, sure. It's stronger than anything he's created in some time.
